issue.title: Bug: [HA] swbusd h2 connection reset errors during HA process crash tests

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium, Log Analyzer noise

### Description of the bug

During HA process-crash tests, Log Analyzer reports `swbusd` h2 protocol errors from `dash-hadpu*` containers:

```text
ERR dash-hadpuX#swbusd: ... ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-from://..."}:
Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection"
```

The test intentionally crashes an HA-related process on one side. When that happens, existing swbus connections to the crashed/restarting peer can be abruptly closed. The reported `h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection` is consistent with that expected connection teardown during the crash/recovery window.

The test function itself passed. This does not currently indicate a functional HA failure; it is a log cleanliness / Log Analyzer filtering issue for intentional process-crash scenarios.

## Triage

The reported failures are from HA process crash tests:

```text
test_crash_active_npu_traffic_on_active[hamgrd]
test_crash_active_npu_traffic_on_standby[pmon]
test_crash_active_npu_traffic_on_standby[bgp]
```

The common error signature is:

```text
Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection"
```

Representative logs:

```shell
ERR dash-hadpu0#swbusd:
ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-from://<peer-ip>:<port>"}:
107: Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection",
details: [], metadata: MetadataMap { headers: {} }.

ERR dash-hadpu1#swbusd:
ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-to://<peer-ip>:<port>"}:
107: Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection",
details: [], metadata: MetadataMap { headers: {} }.

ERR dash-hadpu2#swbusd:
ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-to://<peer-ip>:<port>"}:
107: Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection",
details: [], metadata: MetadataMap { headers: {} }.

ERR dash-hadpu3#swbusd:
ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-from://<peer-ip>:<port>"}:
107: Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection",
details: [], metadata: MetadataMap { headers: {} }.
```

The errors occur across multiple `dash-hadpu*` instances at approximately the same time, which is expected when the test intentionally disrupts the active NPU-side `hamgrd` process and swbus connections to that node reset.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run HA NPU process crash test with `hamgrd` as the crashed process.
2. Let traffic run during the process crash/recovery flow.
3. Inspect Log Analyzer output or NPU syslog.

Example test:

```shell
python3 -m pytest ha/test_ha_npu_process_crash.py \
  --ignore_la_failure
```

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual behavior:

The HA process-crash test passes, but Log Analyzer flags `swbusd` h2 connection teardown logs as errors.

Expected behavior:

Intentional crash/restart tests should not fail Log Analyzer on expected swbus connection reset messages during the crash window.

### Relevant log output

```shell
ERR dash-hadpu0#swbusd: ... ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-from://<IP>:42264"}:
Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection"

ERR dash-hadpu1#swbusd: ... ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-to://<IP>:23606"}:
Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection"

ERR dash-hadpu2#swbusd: ... ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-to://<IP>:23606"}:
Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection"

ERR dash-hadpu3#swbusd: ... ERROR ConnWorker{conn_id="swbs-to://<IP>:23606"}:
Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection"
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell
SONiC master HA build
```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

### Potential Fix

Add a Log Analyzer/test ignore rule for this h2 protocol connection-reset signature during HA process-crash tests.

Suggested scoped ignore:

```text
ERR dash-hadpu\d+#swbusd: .* ERROR ConnWorker\{conn_id="swbs-(from|to)://.*"\}: .* Failed to receive message: status: Unknown, message: "h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection".*
```

Scope the ignore to tests that intentionally crash or restart HA/NPU-side processes, for example:

```text
ha/test_ha_npu_process_crash.py
test_crash_active_npu_traffic_on_active[hamgrd]
test_crash_active_npu_traffic_on_standby[pmon]
test_crash_active_npu_traffic_on_standby[bgp]
```

This keeps unexpected h2 errors visible in normal tests while suppressing expected connection teardown noise during intentional crash/recovery scenarios.

resolution.title: swbus: log receive stream closure as warning
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:

During intentional HA process crash and restart tests, peer swbus connections can close abruptly. Tonic reports these expected transport closures as errors such as:

```text
h2 protocol error: error reading a body from connection
```

The swbus receive loops previously logged every stream error at `ERROR` severity. This caused Log Analyzer failures even though the connection cleanup, route removal, and reconnection paths operated as designed.

This change logs receive-stream closure at `WARN` severity in both `swbus-core` and `swbus-edge`. Error propagation and recovery behavior are unchanged.

Reviewer entry points:

- `crates/swbus-core/src/mux/conn_worker.rs`
- `crates/swbus-edge/src/core_client.rs`

No new dependencies are required.

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/26217

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test improvement

### Approach

#### What is the motivation for this PR?

HA process crash tests intentionally terminate or restart processes and containers. Existing HTTP/2 streams can therefore close with connection reset, broken pipe, or timeout errors.

These events already trigger the expected swbus recovery path:

1. The connection worker exits with a connection error.
2. Routes associated with the connection are unregistered.
3. The connection store marks the connection lost.
4. Client-owned connections reconnect.

Logging the initial stream closure at `ERROR` incorrectly presents this recoverable lifecycle event as a functional failure and causes unnecessary Log Analyzer failures.

#### How did you do it?

Changed the receive-stream closure log from `error!` to `warn!` in:

- The swbus core connection worker.
- The swbus edge client receive loop.

The message was also changed from:

```text
Failed to receive message
```

to:

```text
Connection receive stream closed
```

The returned error, route cleanup, connection-loss handling, and reconnect behavior remain unchanged.

The implementation does not depend on matching Tonic status codes or Hyper error text, which can represent unrelated failures or change between dependency versions.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Unit and integration tests:

```text
cargo test -p swbus-core -p swbus-edge

36 passed; 0 failed
```

Debian packaging:

```text
dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -b -d
```

Successfully built and verified `dash-ha_1.0.0_amd64.deb`.

Physical SmartSwitch validation:

- Deployed the package to `dash-hadpu0` through `dash-hadpu3` on both switches.
- Verified all `swbusd` and `hamgrd` processes were running the updated binaries.
- Verified bidirectional swbus connectivity with 3/3 successful pings in both directions.
- Ran `test_crash_active_npu_traffic_on_active[hamgrd]`.
- HA crash and recovery completed with 133/133 packets received and 0% traffic loss.
- Observed 15 expected HTTP/2 stream closures:
  - Old `ERR/ERROR Failed to receive message` events: 0
  - New `WARNING/WARN Connection receive stream closed` events: 15

The pytest run still reported an unrelated Log Analyzer teardown error from `orchagent` failing to remove referenced HA scope/set objects. No swbus HTTP/2 closure was reported at `ERROR` severity.

#### Any platform specific information?

No. The change applies to generic swbus gRPC stream handling. Physical validation was performed on NVIDIA SN4280 SmartSwitches.

### Documentation

No documentation update is required. This change only corrects log severity and wording; it does not modify public behavior or configuration.
